reviews.title: Absolute dishonesty garbage
reviews.text:
So a move to a new house started to setup the LG TV with Apple TV, because LG, “I own the room”. LG TV has never been on the network and never will be but more about that later. The remote is lost in one of a couple of dozen boxes and I need a temporary remote.

So I downloaded the app and it politely asked me brand of TV and once selected it brazenly displayed a status bar and declared itself connected. It then told me it’s premium features, basically all of them were locked behind a $9.99 a month paywall. I agreed to a 7 day free trial. Then a window popped up wanting to track me across all apps and devices, not happening. I then tried to use the app again and it pops up a request for precise location data. Again I politely refused. Finally it told me that it needed to be on the same WiFi network as the TV in order to work, showing me that it had lied on startup.

I am uninstalling the app and cancelling the subscription and advise anyone else to do the same.

The biggest issue, however, is the price. Even if this was a free app I wouldn’t bother with it, but £9.99 a week is just pure greed and extortion. I can buy a replacement tv remote for less than that (which is exactly what I’ve just done). I don’t usually leave reviews like this but the developers need to learn that it’s not acceptable. Why have Apple even allowed this? Uninstalled.

reviews.title: This app feels incredibly deceptive. Extremely misleading subscription flow.
reviews.text:
It offers a “free trial” and asks you to tap “Enable Free Trial”. Apple then takes you through the normal payment verification process — in my case, even my bank verified a £0 transaction, and everything appears to be successfully activated.

However, when you return to the app, the free trial is NOT enabled. Instead, you are immediately shown the exact same “Enable Free Trial” screen again and asked to go through the payment process once more.

So the app remains unusable, while repeatedly prompting you to authorize the subscription/trial again.

I’m not going to keep pressing the button to find out how many subscription authorizations it lets me create. This kind of flow feels designed to confuse users into signing up and potentially forgetting about recurring charges later.

Whether this is intentional or a serious bug, it is completely unacceptable for an app dealing with subscriptions. Avoid until this is fixed.
